newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent edges up as market monitors Iran news.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent edges up as market monitors Iran news.

text.p: NWE Brent futures were trading moderately higher on Monday as the market kept a close eye on the latest developments concerning Iran, traders said.
May Brent, due to expire on Tuesday, was trading 20 cents up at $18.08 a barrel at 1010 GMT, while the June contract was 19 cents hgigher at $18.26.

Traders said news U.S. and Saudi intelligence had linked a senior Iranian government official to a group of Shiite Moslems suspected of bombing a U.S. military compound in Saudi Arabia last year killing 19 U.S.servicemen had given the market a small boost.

According to a Washington Post report on Sunday, U.S and Arab officials said Brig Ahmad Sherifi, a senior Iranian intelligence officer and a top official in Iran's Revolutionary Guards, met two years before the bombing with Hani Abd Rahim Sayegh, a Saudi Shiite arrested in Canada last month as "a direct participant" in the bombing.
"It's not as if the market's raced up on the news," said one trader. "But everyone's keeping an eye on the story and it's lending some support."
Meanwhile, the EU-Iran row appeared to have receded into the background, although traders said they were monitoring the situation closely.

"The Iran issue is certainly being watched and while the U.S. is trying to push the EU into a sanctions policy, several members are totally against it," GNI energy analyst Leslie Nicholas wrote in his daily report.

May Brent rose as high as $18.30 on Friday on news of a Tehran-Bonn political row sparked by a German court's ruling last Thursday implicating Iranian leaders in the 1992 killing of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
May gas oil was trading 75 cents higher at $164.25 a tonne on a well-supported physical market amid arbitrage opportunities to the Far East.
